title: What If We Captured One Hour of Sunlight Hitting Earth?

scenes.text: What if we caught just one hour of sunlight? It could run the whole world for a year.
More energy from the Sun hits Earth in one hour than all of humanity uses in an entire year.
The Sun showers Earth at about 120,000 terawatts. Humanity burns through roughly 13 terawatts.
That is a gap of roughly 9,000 times, and it arrives every single hour of daylight.
The hard part isn't the supply. It is catching it, storing it, and moving it to where people live.
So the next energy source isn't missing. It is already shining on your roof.

description:
What if we captured one hour of sunlight hitting Earth?
It carries more energy than all of humanity uses in a year, and the Sun delivers about 9,000 times our average demand.
What should we run through next?
thumbnail_text: ONE HOUR OF SUN. ONE YEAR OF POWER.
